newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -FTSE options busy as UK shares jump.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -FTSE options busy as UK shares jump.

text.p: A swift rebound on the London stock market on Wednesday was an invitation for traders to take positions in FTSE 100 index options and futures in preference to stock options, dealers said.

By mid-afternoon the main deals were volatility trades in which an options position is hedged by a futures position. These deals will make money if implied market volatility changes sufficiently causing changes to option premiums.
If UK interest rates go up in the weeks ahead this too will affect option prices by, in general, increasing the value of calls and decreasing the value of puts.

One of the larger deals in FTSE by mid-afternoon was from a buyer of a calendar call spread who also sold futures. The spread was established by selling 1,500 July 4775 calls at about 30p and buying 1,500 September 4775 calls at 80p.
If implied volatility of the market rises, the current 56p will widen owing to changes in the options prices. The spread was hedged by selling September FTSE futures at 4650.

Another deal -- executed by the same broker -- was a put spread which was hedged by a long futures position. It involved selling 1,200 July 4325 puts at 13p, buying 1,200 4525 puts at 48p as well as buying September futures at 4645.

There was also a crossed deal involving a call spread traded against futures. It concerned 500 August 4875 calls traded at 29p against 500 August 5025 calls traded at 9p. The spread was hedged by trading September FTSE futures at 4650.
At 1330 GMT, cash FTSE was up 36.5 at 4632.8 and September futures were up 28 points at 4656.
